messages:
claire: Quick brain-dump: we should build a "shadow-preview" flow for runtime config changes. It would mirror a tiny sampled copy of live requests through the new routing/quotas logic (read-only) to catch behavior that dry-run misses.

zack: would this actually execute batching/cache logic or just simulate routing rules?

claire: actual execution. Mirror path should exercise batching, prefix cache, model selection, etc., but not perform downstream writes or mutate customer state. Think: safe sandbox that still runs the runtime codepaths.

priya: Key safety constraints: 1) preview traffic must be billed to a preview bucket and never count against tenant quotas/SLOs. 2) logs must be redacted by default. 3) per-org preview budget + per-run cap.

infra-bot: AUDIT: preview_created id=prv_5867239999 initiator=claire

leo: API sketch:
POST /api/v1/configs/preview
Body: { config_patch: <patch>, sample_pct: 0.1, duration_sec: 600, max_tokens: 10000 }
Response: { preview_id: "prv_5867239999" }

han: console UX: show preview tile with live diff metrics (preview vs baseline), sample size, estimated cost, abort button, and a promote button that opens the gated-rollout modal.

zack: telemetry gates idea: monitor p95 latency, error_rate, token_cost_per_request, and reroute_ratio. Fail if relative change > config thresholds AND statistical significance (p < 0.01). Show raw sample counts and confidence intervals.

priya: security: redact prompt bodies; display hashed prompt fingerprints + token totals. Allow raw logs only to authorized SREs and encrypt with a preview-only KMS key.

claire: implementation notes: add router flag `mirror_mode=preview_id` that forks requests into preview shards. Preview shards run against a read-only connector shim that returns canned responses for write ops. Preview shards should be capacity-limited so they never affect prod headroom.

leo: warmup: include a cache-prime stage that issues synthetic short-prefix requests so preview caches approximate prod cold/warm state. Surface cache-hit divergence in the UI.

infra-bot: SUGGEST: default sample_pct = 0.1% for new orgs, 1% for enterprise with explicit opt-in above that.

zack: concurrency: allow multiple previews concurrently but warn on overlapping route keys. When promoting, require a lightweight write-fence: fail apply if config version != preview_base_version.

han: CLI example:
```
redwoodctl preview --patch delta.json --sample 0.5 --duration 900
# -> PREVIEW_ID=prv_5867239999
redwoodctl preview-status prv_5867239999
redwoodctl preview-promote prv_5867239999 --canary 5 --auto-rollback true --window 3600
```

priya: billing/quotas: preview runs must have a separate ledger. Do not surface preview cost in tenant billing reports; show it in org admin preview usage only.

claire: rollout behavior: promote should kick off a canary with telemetry checks; platform auto-rollbacks if gates trip. Also record preview telemetry snapshot for 7 days for audits.

leo: edge-cases: model variant mismatch (quantized vs fp16) -> show kernel/variant mismatch warning. long-tail cache divergence -> surface example queries where model chosen differs.

infra-bot: REMINDER: preview start/stop/promote/abort actions must be emitted to audit-stream with initiator and run_id.

zack: next steps: prototype router mirror flag + read-only connector (leo + han, 2w). priya to draft redaction/KMS policy (1w). CLI/console mockups (claire) 1w. dogfood inside infra after phase 1.

claire: thanks — filing tickets and will link them here. :thumbsup:
